correctness.rationale: Exact complex-real Jacobian obtained from original ODE. Two real rank-two phase constraints isolate M-2 zero and M-2 negative radial eigenvalues; a two-complex-scalar determinant yields the quartic. Exact polynomial identities and the positive-root argument make the Routh–Hurwitz condition necessary and sufficient for every M and parameter in scope. At equality an explicit stable-quadratic times imaginary-pair factorization applies. Exact four-agent threshold is 13/18. An included checker separately compares full numerical Jacobians with the characteristic polynomial and tests an exact rational Hurwitz identity (2283 cases). Proof not dependent on finite tests.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary full texts and targeted research-index statements support a genuine gap between known balanced-polygon numerical transverse stability and real-coupling splay-state formulas, versus this exact reactive complex-coupling, shape-dependent criterion. The earlier real-coupling theorem is properly credited; its sign condition cannot imply reactive stabilization for positive real coupling. Residual possible coverage in uninspected complex-coupling stability literature is acknowledged.

value.rationale: An exact complete spectral and normal-attraction classification replaces a sampling-based stability diagnostic for natural noncollinear zero-mean polygons. Its one-scalar shape reduction permits analytic threshold calculations for any M; the explicit four-agent examples exhibit simultaneous attracting and unstable transverse geometry at exactly the same coefficients. This is substantive phase-space information, not mere rescaling, renaming, or finite numerical enumeration.
